title: Discussion: Transformers and Evolution of Large Language Models
topic_name: Transformers and Evolution of Large Language Models
html:
This discussion area is an additional means to interact with the weekly discussion and interactions. Please feel free to discuss our weekly topic live during the class session, via teams during the session, and/or here at any time during the week.

Additionally, groups can choose to present their weekly homework topics here if they choose to do so.

  1. Before the first meeting of the week:
    • Provide a substantive post reflecting on the reading materials and slide deck:
      1. One concept that was interesting to you and how you can apply it to your future career or life.
      2. One concept that was difficult to understand and what made it confusing.
      3. One external resource you found that helped you understand the concept better, along with an explanation of how it helped.
    • (Optional) Contribute to the group aspect of the weekly assignment.
  2. After the first meeting and before the second meeting of the week:
    • View and respond to the course recording.
    • Provide a written version of the in-class activities prior to the second meeting of the week AND
    • Respond to at least one peer to continue the conversation, clarify an idea, or share a relevant resource (you can respond to live session discussion points or online posts).
  3. Complete the weekly assignment.

Weekly Discussion Prompts: Transformers and Evolution of Large Language Models

Use the prompts below to anchor your initial post, guide group collaboration, or prepare your responses:

Prompt 1: The Self-Attention Revolution

  • Context: Prior to 2017, NLP relied on recurrent neural networks (RNNs, LSTMs) that processed text sequentially token-by-token. The Transformer replaced recurrence with multi-head self-attention, enabling complete parallelization during training across GPU clusters.
  • Discussion Question: How did parallel training unlock the massive scaling that produced modern LLMs? What quadratic computational cost does standard self-attention face as sequence lengths grow, and how do modern architectures address it?

Prompt 2: Architecture Divergence: Encoder-Only vs. Decoder-Only

  • Context: The original Transformer was an encoder-decoder sequence-to-sequence model. Over time, the industry bifurcated into encoder-only models (like BERT for understanding and embeddings) and decoder-only models (like GPT for generative autoregression).
  • Discussion Question: Why did decoder-only architectures dominate generative AI, while encoder-only models remained the standard for search embeddings and classification? What trade-offs exist between causal masking and bidirectional attention?

Prompt 3: Emergent Abilities and the Scaling Hypothesis

  • Context: As models scale in parameters, dataset tokens, and compute, they exhibit 'emergent abilities'—sudden jumps in multi-step arithmetic, translation, and code synthesis not observed in smaller models.
  • Discussion Question: Do you believe continuing to scale compute and parameters will lead to General Artificial Intelligence, or will architectures encounter fundamental limits (such as energy, data availability, and synthetic collapse) that require new paradigms?

Prompt 4: Group Homework Topic Presentations (Optional)

  • If your group is choosing to present your weekly assignment findings here on the board, please share your slide link, code/workflow summary, and a brief overview of the problem you solved. Group members must reply within the thread to document individual contributions.
